Name: Origination data schema
Purpose: Defines every field captured at loan/policy origination so a pool is ABS-data-tape-ready from day one rather than retrofitted.
Tests: Schema self-check and dataset validation (validate_schema.py), runs in CI
Notes: v0.1 field list built: 57 fields across 5 entities, 45 critical path. Not yet field-tested - see risk-tools/schema/README.md for what would move it to v1. FIELD-TEST ROUTE NAMED 2026-08-22: EXP-22 is the experiment that would move this from v0.1 to v1 - it runs the full 57-field set against a live origination pipeline, costs each field, and uses validate_schema.py on the output, so a field the validator keeps rejecting surfaces as a schema defect rather than an officer error. Its H3 deliverable is a ranked per-field cost curve, which is what would let an originator adopt the schema incrementally instead of all at once. FIELD REQUIREMENT FROM LC-07 (2026-08-22): LIT-043's discrete-time survival specification needs origination date, censoring status, and an EVENT TYPE that distinguishes default from prepayment, write-off and restructure - competing risks, not a single default flag. Check the 57-field list carries all four.

Name: Underwriting engine
Purpose: Scores a borrower or group from origination data plus community signals; produces a decision, a limit and a price.
Tests: Monotonicity in leverage; every decline/refer carries a reason (test_toolchain.py, CI)
Notes: Rules-based scorecard running against synthetic RT-1 data. Emits a band, a limit and the reasons in both directions - an unexplained decline is not defensible under the consumer-protection framing in LIT-014. Two rules only exist because the schema captures cycle length and livelihood: the share-out constraint and correlated agricultural exposure. Uncalibrated; no ML until there is a repayment history to backtest this baseline against.

Name: Monitoring and early-warning system
Purpose: Tracks DPD, delinquency and claim patterns against expectation; raises alerts before losses crystallise.
Notes: Monitor running over the RT-1 event stream: PAR30/PAR90, arrears concentration by group, region and originator, and threshold alerts with --as-of for point-in-time evaluation. Demonstrated to fire while under 20% of eventual write-offs have been booked - roughly 4-7 months of lead in the synthetic run. Thresholds are judgement, not estimates.

Name: Impact evaluation module
Purpose: Randomisation infrastructure and pre-registered analysis for pilot evaluation with an academic partner.
Tests: None yet - simulation-based power checks planned
Notes: Design must be fixed and pre-registered before enrolment. Choosing the estimator after seeing outcomes is how impact claims lose credibility.

Name: Securitisation cash-flow model
Purpose: Waterfall model with loss and prepayment simulation; sizes tranches and tests the first-loss layer.
Tests: Waterfall conservation assertion on every path; deterministic seed
Notes: Synthetic scaffold running: pool generator, single-factor correlated loss model, sequential waterfall, six macro stress scenarios. Uncalibrated - outputs are structural, not evidential. Already yields a derived OQ-2 answer via --sweep: fixed costs dominate the junior tranche below roughly USD 5m and flatten around USD 20-40m. CALIBRATION ROUTE NAMED 2026-08-22: EXP-25's respec includes an explicit step to recover a single-factor asset correlation from partner loan panels, which is exactly the input this model currently sweeps. Until that lands the correlation sweep stays the honest output. DISCLOSURE REQUIREMENT FROM LC-07 (2026-08-22): LIT-042 (SR 11-7) says conservatism must be substantiated, and that an extreme point on a modelled distribution is not conservative if the distribution is misspecified. The correlation sweep is honest precisely because it does not claim a conservative point estimate - keep it that way, and say so when the model is published. OQ-18 RAISED 2026-08-22: the business plan assumes a regional multi-originator pool, but the correlation channel that predicts trouble is market-level, so pooling lenders within one market may concentrate rather than diversify. Until EXP-25 settles it, do not model a regional multi-originator pool as diversified.

Name: Unit-economics model
Purpose: Models the structuring company's own P&L across three scenarios to answer OQ-10: is there a credible path to at-scale profitability? Deal- and venture-level net margin, break-even pool size, deals-to-breakeven, the pilot-breakeven yardstick on the flagship trio, and sensitivity to loss and fee compression.
Tests: P&L identity (revenue-cost=margin), economies of scale, scenario ordering, gate consistency (test_toolchain.py, CI)
Notes: Deterministic closed-form P&L over Worst/Likely/Best scenarios. GATE (OQ-10, set 2026-08-02) = structuring layer covers its own costs within 3y at reachable scale; KPIs tracked = operating margin (t.30%) and return on capital-at-risk (t.15%); investor tranche returns are the binding constraint. 5/23 drivers SOURCED (MIX 2017-18, Symbiotics 2019, Convergence, OECD - LIT-016..019), 18 ASSUMED. Likely case passes the gate and meets both KPIs but the junior tranche needs concessional pricing; pilots sit 14-50x below break-even. Not calibrated - outputs describe the model, not the asset class. Separate from RT-5, which owns the loss distribution.

Name: Collective facility risk model
Purpose: Models a lender's loss distribution on a facility to a producer collective that on-lends to members and markets their crop. Yield and price factors drive member debt-service cover, cover drives PD, defaults carry a residual correlation, forward-sale shortfall and side-selling cost the collective, and the collective's net cash flow is the first-loss buffer. Outputs EL, UL, stress scenarios, one-at-a-time sensitivities and an illustrative tranche cut.
Stack: Python (numpy) reference; JavaScript port runs the dashboard tab
Tests: PD-curve anchor and monotonicity; golden EL identity; direction of response to shocks; tranche conservation; loss bounds; JS/Python parity (test_rt7.py, CI)
Blocked_By: DS-07; DS-08 for calibration (all catalogue rows Proposed); RT-5 for a cash waterfall
Notes: v0.1 was the 2026-10-07 sfv_risk_models prototype, archived verbatim under archive/prototype-2026-10/. Its loss numbers did not respond to climate or price at all: PD was computed on average revenue, one yield draw served every path, collective cash flow could never be negative and defaults were independent. v0.2 repairs the chain and makes the two correlation channels EXP-25 identifies explicit - environmental (yield and price through DSCR) and institutional (residual_correlation). UNCALIBRATED: every row of data/rt7-parameters.csv is Basis assumption; LIT-035 and LIT-036/037 are reference points, not estimates. FIRST STRUCTURAL FINDING (v0.2 defaults, seed 42): the tail is delivery risk, not credit risk - a forward book without delivery enforcement turns a price spike into the largest loss the facility can take, and side_sell_elasticity or price_vol is the top sensitivity in every region. Vietnam is a modelling case only (decision 2026-10-08, OQ-22 open). Interactive on the dashboard's Collective model tab; headline rows in data/rt7-region-results.csv and data/rt7-sensitivity.csv.
